decision.explanation: Different from every known condition. The distance ranking initially favors C03, and 3.916 dB versus C03's 6.197-dB separation from other references is supportive. However, the measurements and physical-frequency figures conflict decisively: Q01 is an approximately 16-kHz-dominated, high-band signal, whereas C03 is a strongly 5.3-Hz-dominated low-band periodic signal. C01 and C02 share the near-16-kHz ridge but have much lower high-band fractions and centroids and stronger low-frequency structures. All reports have identical 10-s duration, 44.1-kHz sampling, 0.1-Hz FFT spacing and 43.07-Hz Welch spacing, so these differences are not coverage, sampling-rate, or resolution artifacts. Unknown acquisition gain limits interpretation of absolute FS levels, but gain cannot account for the markedly different normalized band-power distributions, harmonic emphasis, periodicity, or time-frequency patterns.
